- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or 1.5x prior 7-day average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 5–15% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows >10% deviation from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend, not 30-day trend.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa) within 3 days, model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment shift.
- If forecast is >2.5x the 14-day average and sentiment is neutral or mixed, reduce forecast by 30–50% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For low sentiment (≤0.33) and low price history, model underestimates; add 10–20% to forecast to account for hidden demand or policy surprises.
